Explain mapper results row by row

Source: R/explain-map.R
explain_map.Rd

explain_map() takes the output of grim_map(), grimmer_map(), or debit_map() and adds an explanation column: the calculation behind each row's result in plain words, as printed by grim_explain(), grimmer_explain(), and debit_explain() for a single case. It also takes the output of the sequence and total-n mappers built on them, such as grim_map_seq().

To read the explanations, use explain_print().

Usage

explain_map(data, ...)

Arguments

data

Data frame returned by one of the mappers named above.

...

Must be empty for scrutiny's methods; methods for other classes may use them.

Value

data with an explanation column, a string per row.

Details

Each row is tested again from its own values and the settings of the mapper call, such as rounding and x_meaning. If the result differs from the row's consistency value, the row must have been changed after testing, and explain_map() throws an error.

DEBIT explanations cover formula = "exact" only.

Examples

pigs1 |>
  grim_map(digits_x = 2, items_averaged = 1, data_type = "integer") |>
  dplyr::filter(!consistency) |>
  explain_map()
#> # A tibble: 8 × 8
#> # GRIM: default settings
#>       x     n items_averaged data_type digits_x consistency exp_incon
#>   <dbl> <int>          <int> <chr>        <int> <lgl>           <dbl>
#> 1  4.74    25              1 integer          2 FALSE            0.75
#> 2  5.23    29              1 integer          2 FALSE            0.71
#> 3  2.57    24              1 integer          2 FALSE            0.72
#> 4  6.77    27              1 integer          2 FALSE            0.73
#> 5  7.01    29              1 integer          2 FALSE            0.71
#> 6  3.14    27              1 integer          2 FALSE            0.73
#> 7  6.89    31              1 integer          2 FALSE            0.69
#> 8  0.24    28              1 integer          2 FALSE            0.72
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: explanation <chr>
